turns.text: Hey Lloyd, quick question about my research notes. I'm finalizing the comparison section for the WFM paper.
Sure, Alan. What specifically do you need help with in that section?
I need to verify the baselines. I wrote down that WFM is compared against GraphRAG, LightRAG, HippoRAG 2, and GFM-RAG in a single results table.
Got it. That's a solid set of baselines. Do you need me to format that into a table structure for you?
No, just checking if that list looks right in my notes. Also, did my package for the new mechanical keyboard arrive?

I don't have access to your real-time shipping updates, but you can check your email for the tracking number. Regarding the paper, the list seems consistent with recent retrieval-augmented generation benchmarks.
Cool. I'll check the tracking. Let's stick to the paper for now. I want to make sure the narrative flows well around those baselines.
Understood. We can work on the narrative flow whenever you're ready.
Lloyd, I've been looking at the methodology section again. There's a specific detail about how WFM handles seeding.
Okay, what's the detail you're concerned about?
I want to clarify that WFM does not add mechanisms to seed resolution, relying on query to seed entity/passage resolution.
Noted. That distinction is important for the technical accuracy of the paper.
Yeah. I think I need to emphasize that in the abstract. By the way, it's raining hard here. Any good indoor movie recommendations?
Since you're working on a dense paper, maybe something light? *The Grand Budapest Hotel* is a good visual palate cleanser.
I'll put that on the list. Back to work. I need to rewrite the paragraph on resolution to reflect the note I just gave you.
Sounds good. I can help draft that paragraph if you paste the current version.
